paths.description: Homepage and primary search entry, representing landing, theming, responsive layout, network/performance and primary action.
Primary search-results journey using a representative query; bot challenge persisted after a manual visual solve attempt.
Interactive settings/form template covering localization, native controls, preferences and accountless cloud-save affordance.
Long-form public content template covering responsive reading, metadata, no-JS rendering and performance.
Unknown-route/network-recovery probe; server converted it into a search and the anti-bot gate blocked further recovery-state inspection.

findings.summary: The anti-bot challenge has no accessible non-visual completion path.
findings.evidence: The search screenshot shows a required image-classification puzzle. The rendered DOM uses clickable div tiles with background images and no accessible names/roles; the HTML fallback uses images with alt=" ". Search could not be completed.
findings.suggestedFix: Offer an equivalent non-visual verification method, give the challenge a labelled dialog structure, and expose each selectable option with an accessible name and state.

findings.summary: Largest Contentful Paint is slow on both primary templates.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse measured LCP at 6.2 s on the homepage and 7.9 s on the privacy page, both well outside the good threshold; performance scores were 69 and 73.
findings.suggestedFix: Prioritise the LCP resource, reduce render-blocking styles and font work, and defer below-fold application payloads.

findings.summary: The homepage has a heavy critical delivery path.
findings.evidence: HAR captured 108 requests and 2,028,477 transferred bytes, including 8 parser-inserted very-high-priority stylesheets and 585,909 font bytes; Lighthouse flags render blocking on the privacy template.
findings.suggestedFix: Consolidate and inline only critical CSS, reduce font families/weights, preload only the actual LCP dependencies, and defer non-critical styles.

findings.summary: Substantial unused and legacy JavaScript ships on initial load.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse estimates 117 KiB unused JavaScript and 21 KiB legacy JavaScript on the homepage, and 176 KiB unused plus 14 KiB legacy JavaScript on /privacy.
findings.suggestedFix: Route-split page code, remove unnecessary polyfills for the supported Baseline, and load below-fold/interactive modules on demand.

findings.summary: Some images are rendered with incorrect aspect ratios and weak sizing metadata.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse fails the image aspect-ratio audit. The image probe reports 51 of 67 images without both dimensions, although many are hidden/decorative and did not produce homepage CLS.
findings.suggestedFix: Give rendered images intrinsic width/height or aspect-ratio matching the source and remove hidden duplicate image markup from the initial DOM.

findings.summary: Homepage heading levels do not form a coherent hierarchy.
findings.evidence: The DOM has two H1 elements and jumps from H3 to H6 ("Get our free browser today"); Lighthouse fails heading-order.
findings.suggestedFix: Use one page H1 and assign section headings by document hierarchy rather than visual size.

findings.summary: Several homepage links do not provide descriptive link text.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse SEO reports 8 links with non-descriptive text.
findings.suggestedFix: Give each link concise visible or accessible text that describes its destination without surrounding context.

findings.summary: The CSP permits both unsafe-inline and unsafe-eval for scripts.
findings.evidence: The headers primitive confirms HTTPS, HSTS, nosniff and frame protections, but script-src includes unsafe-inline and unsafe-eval, weakening XSS mitigation.
findings.suggestedFix: Move inline code to nonce/hash-authorised scripts, remove eval-dependent code, and adopt a strict nonce-based CSP with Trusted Types where applicable.

findings.summary: The homepage’s substantive content is largely unavailable without JavaScript.
findings.evidence: Discoverability measured only 2% raw-to-rendered content coverage and classified the homepage as a JS shell; /privacy reaches 100%, showing the content template can server-render.
findings.suggestedFix: Server-render the homepage’s meaningful headings, copy, navigation and primary search form, then hydrate optional interactions progressively.

findings.summary: The published sitemap contains malformed and mistyped entries.
findings.evidence: The fetched sitemap includes lastmod 2025-03-282 for /about and an extra closing </url> around /pro, making indexing signals unreliable.
findings.suggestedFix: Generate sitemap.xml from validated route data, emit valid ISO dates, and validate the XML in CI.

findings.summary: The blocking anti-bot overlay is custom div markup rather than a semantic modal primitive.
findings.evidence: The challenge DOM is a .anomaly-modal__mask/.modal div tree without <dialog>, role=dialog, aria-modal or an explicit accessible label.
findings.suggestedFix: Implement the challenge with <dialog> (or an equivalent correctly labelled modal pattern), trap and restore focus, and provide a clear escape/recovery path.

findings.summary: No container-query adaptation was found in the homepage component styles.
findings.evidence: A CSSOM probe found zero @container rules even though the homepage reuses search, cards, tabs and promotional modules at varied widths; viewport layouts themselves did reflow without overflow.
findings.suggestedFix: Use container-type and targeted @container rules for reusable modules whose composition depends on available component width.

findings.summary: No View Transition integration was found for state or route changes.
findings.evidence: The CSSOM probe found no view-transition rules and route changes use conventional navigation; no transition was visible in sampled states.
findings.suggestedFix: Add same-document transitions for major state changes and cross-document view transitions for compatible first-party routes, while preserving reduced-motion handling.

findings.summary: Initial resource weight is disproportionate for a search landing page.
findings.evidence: The homepage transfers 2.03 MB: 512 KB images, 586 KB fonts and 781 KB scripts. The image probe reports 63 below-fold images without lazy loading and 23 legacy-format images.
findings.suggestedFix: Do not load below-fold promotional media until near viewport, use responsive AVIF/WebP sources, subset fonts, and set a landing-page transfer budget.

findings.summary: The bot-block state gives no accessible way to recover and complete search.
findings.evidence: Both JavaScript and HTML search paths stop at the visual duck puzzle. The JS state offers only Submit; the HTML fallback only offers an email code when images fail, not an immediate equivalent completion path.
findings.suggestedFix: Provide a keyboard and screen-reader operable alternative, a retry/support path, and preserve the submitted query through recovery.

findings.summary: Several primary controls have sub-44px touch targets.
findings.evidence: The focus/geometry probe measured the menu and search submit controls at 32×32 px, AI settings at 38×38 px, and toggle inner buttons at 18×18 px; focus indicators were generally present.
findings.suggestedFix: Expand interactive hit areas to at least 44×44 CSS px without enlarging icons, and retain the visible focus treatment.

findings.summary: Touch target sizing falls short despite otherwise good mobile reflow.
findings.evidence: Mobile layouts have no horizontal overflow and allow scaling, but the geometry probe finds multiple 18–38px controls on the primary homepage.
findings.suggestedFix: Increase the clickable area around icon controls to 44×44 CSS px and verify spacing at 200% zoom.

findings.summary: Strong baseline headers are undermined by permissive script execution policy.
findings.evidence: HSTS, X-Frame-Options, nosniff, Referrer-Policy and Permissions-Policy are present, but CSP allows unsafe-inline/unsafe-eval and no Trusted Types requirement was observed.
findings.suggestedFix: Tighten script-src with nonces/hashes, remove unsafe-eval, and add require-trusted-types-for script after compatibility testing.

findings.summary: Below-fold media and fonts consume most of the landing-page transfer budget up front.
findings.evidence: Fonts, images and scripts account for about 1.88 MB of 2.03 MB transferred; 63 below-fold images were present without lazy loading. Third-party transfer was low at 4,951 bytes.
findings.suggestedFix: Lazy-load or conditionally import below-fold promotional modules and media; retain the current low third-party footprint.

taskList.title: Make anti-bot verification accessible and recoverable
Fix LCP and reduce the critical request/font/style path
Server-render meaningful homepage content and the core search form
Lazy-load below-fold media and trim initial JavaScript/font weight
Replace unsafe CSP script allowances with nonces/hashes
Correct heading hierarchy, image sizing and link names
Adopt component queries and View Transitions where they improve reused UI
